core_obligations: Reduce to the case I_1 cap I_2 = 0 by replacing R and M by their quotients (proof lines 3959-3961).
Fix an ideal J and use flatness of M/I_1 M over R/I_1 to obtain the injection J/(J cap I_1) tensor M to M/I_1 M (proof lines 3962-3970).
Draw the commutative diagram comparing J tensor M, M and M/I_1 M and reduce the verification to the injectivity of (J cap I_1) tensor M to M (proof lines 3971-3983).
Identify (J cap I_1) tensor M with J' tensor over R/I_2 with M/I_2 M by the vanishing of the intersection and conclude injectivity from the second flatness hypothesis (proof lines 3983-3989).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a zero intersection (proof lines 3959-3961).
First injection from flatness modulo I_1 (proof lines 3962-3970).
Glue along the commutative diagram (proof lines 3971-3983).
Second injection from flatness modulo I_2 and conclude (proof lines 3983-3990).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that flatness of a module modulo two ideals implies flatness modulo their intersection, and the proof is a 32-line computation with the equational criterion for flatness. It reduces to the case where the intersection is zero, then for an ideal J produces, by the flatness over the two quotients, two injections into the two quotients of M, glues them along a commutative diagram to show that the multiplication map J tensor M to M is injective, and concludes flatness. The gluing diagram and the use of the two flatness hypotheses are the substance.
